title: Grandma's Moist Pumpkin Bread
excerpt: When autumn leaves gather by the kitchen door, this pumpkin bread is the loaf Grandma always seemed to have cooling on the counter. Its tender crumb, warm cinnamon spice, and optional handfuls of chocolate chips or walnuts make every slice feel like a cozy visit from home.

Why You'll Love This Pumpkin Bread

  • This pumpkin bread has a tender, moist crumb and plenty of warm cinnamon spice.
  • It comes together with simple pantry ingredients and just 15 minutes of prep.
  • Optional chocolate chips or walnuts let you make each loaf your own.
  • A slice is lovely with morning coffee, afternoon tea, or a glass of cold milk.
  • The cozy pumpkin flavor makes it a welcome treat throughout the autumn season.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients for a warmly spiced loaf that tastes like it came from Grandma's kitchen.

  • All-purpose flour - 1 3/4 cups
  • Baking soda - 1 teaspoon
  • Baking powder - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Salt - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Ground cinnamon - 1 1/2 teaspoons
  • Ground nutmeg - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Ground ginger - 1/4 teaspoon
  • Pumpkin puree - 1 cup
  • Granulated sugar - 1/2 cup
  • Packed light brown sugar - 1/2 cup
  • Vegetable oil - 1/2 cup
  • Large eggs - 2
  • Vanilla extract - 1 teaspoon
  • Semisweet chocolate chips - 1/2 cup, optional
  • Chopped walnuts - 1/2 cup, optional

How to Make Pumpkin Bread

Set aside 15 minutes for prep, about 60 minutes for baking, and a little extra time for the loaf to cool before slicing. That resting time helps the crumb finish setting so each slice holds together beautifully.

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat the oven to 350°F. Let it heat fully while you prepare the batter so the loaf begins baking at the proper temperature.

Step 2: Prepare the Pan

Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan thoroughly. Pay special attention to the corners so the cooled loaf releases easily.

Step 3: Whisk the Dry Ingredients

In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger. This distributes the leaveners and spices throughout the flour.

Step 4: Mix the Wet Ingredients

In a large bowl, whisk the pumpkin puree, granulated sugar, brown sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla until smooth and evenly combined.

Step 5: Combine the Batter

Stir the dry ingredients into the pumpkin mixture until just combined. Stop mixing as soon as no dry streaks remain to keep the loaf tender.

Step 6: Add Optional Favorites

Fold in the chocolate chips or walnuts if using. A gentle stir keeps the add-ins evenly distributed without overworking the batter.

Step 7: Fill the Pan

Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan. Smooth the top gently with a spoon so the loaf bakes evenly.

Step 8: Bake the Loaf

Bake the loaf for 55 to 65 minutes. It is ready when the center is set and a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.

Step 9: Rest in the Pan

Cool the loaf in the pan for 15 minutes. This brief rest helps the warm loaf firm up before it is moved.

Step 10: Cool on a Rack

Transfer the loaf to a wire rack to cool completely. Allowing it to finish cooling prevents a gummy texture and makes slicing easier.

Step 11: Slice and Serve

Slice the cooled pumpkin bread before serving. Use a serrated knife and gentle sawing motions for neat slices.

Pro Tips for Making Pumpkin Bread

  • Measure the flour by spooning it into a measuring cup and leveling the top to avoid a dense loaf.
  • Use pumpkin puree rather than pumpkin pie filling, since the recipe already includes its own sugar and spices.
  • Do not overmix after adding the flour. A few small lumps are perfectly fine.
  • Let the loaf cool completely before storing it so condensation does not make the crust damp.
  • For even slices, use a sharp serrated knife and wipe it clean between cuts.

How to Serve Pumpkin Bread

  • Serve slices slightly warm with a little butter or cream cheese.
  • Add a handful of chocolate chips when you want a sweeter, treat-like loaf.
  • Choose walnuts for a pleasant nutty crunch and extra texture.
  • Pair a slice with coffee, tea, or warm milk for a comforting snack.
  • Set the loaf on a family breakfast or dessert table and let everyone help themselves.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool the pumpkin bread completely before wrapping it tightly or placing it in an airtight container.
  • Keep it at room temperature for up to 3 days in a cool, dry spot.
  • For longer freshness, refrigerate the wrapped loaf for up to 1 week.

Freezing

  • Wrap the whole loaf or individual slices tightly in plastic wrap, then place them in a freezer-safe bag or container.
  • Freeze for up to 3 months and label the package with the date.
  • Thaw the loaf overnight in the refrigerator or thaw individual slices at room temperature.

Reheating

  • Warm an individual slice in the microwave for 10 to 15 seconds if desired.
  • For a whole loaf, let it thaw first, then warm it in a 300°F oven until gently heated.
  • Keep an eye on the bread while warming so the edges do not dry out.

Final Thoughts

This moist pumpkin bread is the kind of simple, warmly spiced treat that makes an ordinary day feel a little more special.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for baking and enjoying this cozy loaf.

Can I use homemade pumpkin puree?

Yes, homemade pumpkin puree works well as long as it has a similar thick consistency to canned puree. If it seems watery, drain it briefly before measuring.

Why did my pumpkin bread sink in the middle?

A loaf can sink if the batter is overmixed, the oven temperature is too low, or the bread is removed before the center has fully set. Bake until the center is firm and a toothpick shows only a few moist crumbs.

Can I make this pumpkin bread without the optional add-ins?

Absolutely. The loaf is delicious on its own, with the pumpkin and warm spices taking center stage.

How should I keep pumpkin bread moist?

Cool it completely, then wrap it tightly or store it in an airtight container. Keeping it away from air will help preserve its tender texture.
